quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Depend on road signs to find your way.
Only know generally where your destination is.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip before you leave. Check the location on a map before you start driving. Don't start with only a rough idea of where you are going.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer right to escape. Don't steer left because the other driver might swerve left too, and you'll still crash. Brake hard. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Broken white lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing light means stop. Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before on residential streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Cars are often hidden there. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets. Signal five seconds ahead on freeways.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Don't make sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and don't use cruise control.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection with a green light, but oncoming traffic is heavy. You should:

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: If the light is green and it's safe, you can move into the center of the intersection to prepare to turn left. Wait there until oncoming traffic passes, then complete your turn.

questions.question: Drivers should watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They can move quickly and have less noticeable lighting. Stay alert to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: Regulatory signs tell drivers:

options.text: What they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.

questions.correctAnswerText: What they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They show speed limits, no passing zones, no turns, and other driving rules.

questions.question: When a vehicle ahead has high beams on, look toward which part of the road?
questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the headlights and helps you stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Steer in the direction the vehicle is skidding.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay for drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with one rider.
When passing a motorcycle, change lanes completely.
A motorcycle's brake lights always turn on when it slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing a motorcycle, change lanes completely.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full width of a lane. Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow, what should you do?

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn left after giving way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed on a road under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed for ideal conditions. You can drive slower, but not faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, and bad weather.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. The tracks cross at a steep angle, and the bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. This sign warns that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: Who causes most fatal crashes between large trucks and passenger vehicles?

options.text: The driver of the passenger vehicle.
Animals on the road cause them.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver of the passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: In more than 70 percent of fatal crashes between a passenger vehicle and a truck, the passenger vehicle driver caused it. Keep extra space between your vehicle and large trucks.
